# The `typing` job's toolchain, hash-pinned (#1548): mypy and
# homeassistant-stubs at the pair tests/typing_budgets.json records, the
# ruler's third-party names, and everything homeassistant-stubs resolves them
# to, frozen at the resolution CI's typing job installed before this file
# existed. `python3 tests/typing_ruler.py` refuses this file when its mypy or
# homeassistant-stubs pin disagrees with the recorded pair, or when a
# third-party name is missing from it.
#
# Linux only. It is resolved for linux x86_64, so on macOS bleak's pyobjc
# dependencies are not in it and hash-checking mode refuses the install. One
# package (PyRIC) has no wheel and builds from source under
# tests/requirements-build.txt.
#
# Regenerate after the pair moves in tests/typing_budgets.json:
#   python3 tests/typing_ruler.py --print-requirements \
#     | uv pip compile - --python-version 3.14.7 \
#       --python-platform x86_64-manylinux_2_28 --generate-hashes \
#       --no-header --no-annotate --override <overrides> -o <body>
# and replace everything below the blank line that ends this header.
#
# <overrides> holds cryptography==50.0.1 and pyopenssl==26.4.0. homeassistant
# pins cryptography==48.0.1, which carries three advisories (Dependabot 66, 69
# and 70), and pyopenssl 26.2.0 caps it below 49. mypy imports neither, so the
# override changes no measured number. Because homeassistant's own pin now
# disagrees with the lock, CI installs it with --no-deps: this file is already
# the full resolution. Drop the override once homeassistant pins >= 50.
